limits_note: 200 GB/dataset; 50 top-level files per dataset (use a directory tree or a ZIP. Kaggle unzips archives server-side and the unzipped size counts); each new version adds a full copy so versioned datasets consume quota per version and old versions cannot be deleted (documented user complaint, unresolved); dynamic rate limiting on the API (HTTP 429). Dataset ingestion of a >100 GB upload via the web UI/API is flaky. Kaggle staff recommend creating from a remote URL or GCS bucket instead.

extras.quota_verbatim: 200 GB per dataset (hard, public or private), 50 top-level files per dataset, 200 GB max total PRIVATE datasets. There is NO documented aggregate cap on public datasets — the docs' 'Technical Specifications' section states only '200GB per dataset limit', '200GB max private datasets', 'A max of 50 top-level files'. Public total is therefore effectively unlimited per account, and the 200 GB/dataset ceiling is raised on request (see quota-program candidate).
extras.limits_verbatim: 200 GB/dataset; 50 top-level files per dataset (use a directory tree or a ZIP — Kaggle unzips archives server-side and the unzipped size counts); each new version adds a full copy so versioned datasets consume quota per version and old versions cannot be deleted (documented user complaint, unresolved); dynamic rate limiting on the API (HTTP 429). Dataset ingestion of a >100 GB upload via the web UI/API is flaky — Kaggle staff recommend creating from a remote URL or GCS bucket instead.
extras.egress_verbatim: Free and CDN-backed: the download endpoint 302s to a signed storage.googleapis.com URL (Google Cloud Storage), which is Fastly/Google-fronted. No egress quota documented, no per-GB charge, no auth needed for public datasets.
extras.chaining_verbatim: 200 GB x unlimited public datasets x unlimited free accounts. Live proof of the unlimited-public side: one account holds 23 public datasets totalling 1,197.7 GB with a largest single dataset of 163.0 GB (API-verified) — i.e. 6x over the 200 GB 'private quota' figure, so the private quota demonstrably does not apply to public datasets. Multiply again by Kaggle Organizations (a dataset can be owned by an org the account belongs to) and by the free quota-request program for >200 GB single datasets.
extras.tooling_verbatim: kagglehub (pip install kagglehub, official, github.com/Kaggle/kagglehub) — resolves public datasets with NO credentials; kaggle-api CLI (`kaggle datasets download -d owner/slug`); plain HTTPS + curl/wget against /api/v1/datasets/download/<owner>/<slug>; rclone can front the signed GCS URL with an HTTP remote.
